{
  "thinking": "Blank table, so we need to pick an animal and plan it. A fish is easy to read from its outline, and the tail fin makes it recognizable. I'll grab the pad and sketch a simple fish facing right, starting at the tail.",
  "say": "Let's do a fish, facing right, with a proper tail fin. Its outline should be easy to read. I'm sketching it on the pad now, so shout if you'd rather do something else.",
  "to": "everyone",
  "eagerness": 7,
  "pad": "take",
  "sketch_clear": true,
  "sketch": [
    {"type": "label", "x": 5, "y": 3, "text": "START"},
    {"type": "curve", "points": [[6, 9], [10, 7], [15, 6.5], [20, 7.5], [23, 10]]},
    {"type": "curve", "points": [[23, 10], [20, 12.5], [15, 13.5], [10, 13], [6, 11]]},
    {"type": "curve", "points": [[6, 9], [3, 6], [2, 10], [3, 12], [6, 11]]},
    {"type": "label", "x": 20, "y": 9, "text": "eye"}
  ],
  "do": "stop",
  "notes": "Plan: fish facing right. Stroke 1 = top of body from tail-top to nose; stroke 2 = belly back to tail-bottom (closes outline); stroke 3 = tail fin. START is at the tail top-left. Pad is with me. Next: trace stroke 1 to lay START, then others. Table is still empty."
}
